Umi is comparing a possibility with lively, focused curiosity. His eyes quickly find a clue off to one side; the attention draws his head and upper chest a little toward it, with his broad curled supporting paw, bent elbow and shoulder making one comfortable connected adjustment under the chin. The other paw gives grounded support. He briefly considers what he sees, softly tightens his small thoughtful mouth, then gives a quick searching glance back and settles into his original pondering pose. The small turns are completed promptly at ordinary alert speed, with readable living pauses between them, rather than a tiny turn stretched across the whole shot. Let the torso's supported change of weight make the head and paws feel connected. A little scarf-tip and folded-ear lag follows the same thought and stops naturally; the lower cape stays draped. The supporting paw keeps its full rounded volume and plausible light chin contact, with its back toward us; it never opens into a palm display. One quick natural blink has clear dark eyelid curves inside the same sockets, with separate gray brows above. This is still quiet thought, not a celebration. Arrive naturally at the supplied original chin-supported pose with compatible breathing and movement direction for the loop; no final frozen beat or snap back.

Keep each main small attention change decisive, around0.2–0.4seconds, separated by short thoughtful living pauses rather than a2–3second head drift. Eyes find the idea, and the supported head/chest follow together. Preserve full rounded paw-to-chin contact through the change; no sliding away, shrinking paw or palm display. The single cape stays weighted and draped, and the scarf has only a small prompt after-settle, never a wind-like horizontal flare.
